doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

chapter: Free playing, time and the Classic Jazz Trio
title: Classic Jazz Trio and the Columbia Halloween party
summary: His new tuba-piano-drums trio with Billy Hart, and an upcoming Columbia event hosted by Robert O'Meally.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Any new hats you’re going to be wearing in the near future?
Yeah I’ve got a great hat, that I mean it’s an old hat but it’s new to me. It is the Classic Jazz Trio.
The Classic Jazz Trio, with tuba?
Except with tuba. Tuba bass, piano and drums.

I have the Classic Jazz Trio except it’s been bass, drums and piano, coming out from Oscar Peterson to Tatum to Ahmad Jamal. It’s got influences of a lot of that but it’s just with the tuba. Billy Hart’s playing drums. We did a gig recently and we got reviews from the Times and the Voice and everything, it was really fantastic. And we’re going to be doing something else up at Columbia come, if you’re available come on into the city, please. The 31st is going to be a party. Columbia has this annual Halloween party. Dr. Robert O’Meally up at Columbia School of Jazz Studies.

Where he’s doing comparison things between jazz and the improvisational approach of jazz and the improvisational approach of jazz writing and people like Richard Wright and Zora Neale Hurston and people like that, how they have an improvisational approach to their writing skills. And he does a lot of that. And he also presents jazz things, he has a whole jazz program through the course of the year and he’s asked me to perform for his Halloween party. Last year they did that it was Sun Ra. Right. It was Sun Ra’s band that is. And so I feel real honored. It’s going to be a great time.

It’s going to be a great time. We’re going to be doing music from Simone to my compositions to Second Line, you know, again reaching forward and reaching back so the techniques that I need to play a Simone type tune or a Charles Tollver “Ruthie’s
Heart” type tune, and also the techniques going backwards and playing a second line type presentation.
